newsitem.title: FRANCE: France Telecom chairman sees share listing in 1997.
newsitem.headline: France Telecom chairman sees share listing in 1997.

text.p: France Telecom chairman Michel Bon said in a newspaper interview on Monday that he expected the state-owned telecommunications group to list shares on the Paris bourse in mid-April 1997.
"If market conditions are favourable, we're planning to open up the capital in the second half of April 1997...It will take the classic form of a public share offering," he told Les Echos.

Even at the low end of the valuation range for the telecom operator -- valued at between 100 and 200 billion francs ($19.6-$39.2 billion) -- the market would not be able to absorb 49 percent in one go and share sales would have to be carried out in two stages, he said.
Bon said he expected France Telecom and Deutsche Telekom to take cross-holdings once their shares were listed. "We could then pursue our plans for cross-shareholdings," he said.

Bon said a transfer of 37.5 billion francs by France Telecom to the government to cover pension liabilities would "leave us the most indebted European operator." He said the group's debt would exceed 100 billion francs and be greater than its equity.

He said that if the payment were made in a lump sum on January 1, it would take some two billion francs off the group's results. France Telecom earned 17 billion francs before taxes in 1995. ($ = 5.097 French Francs)
